newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan ruling party drafts China peace treaty.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan ruling party drafts China peace treaty.

text.p: Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party completed the draft of a treaty for peace with China on Monday, proposing talks to end a 17-month impasse in relations between the long-time rivals, state radio reported.
A group of professors commissioned by the party completed the draft on Monday, the radio said.

"Under the draft, the two sides will promise not to hold military exercises in nearby seas, will publicise their defence budgets and will station representative delegations in each other's territory," the radio reported.
"The draft will help the two sides reach reunification in peaceful ways," it said.

The draft, calling for an exchange of representatives to discuss a possible treaty, marks a new attempt by Taiwan to resume contacts with China after a breakdown in what had had been slowly warming unofficial ties.
China has said talks cannot resume unless Taiwan shows signs of "sincerity", citing abandonment of its quest for a United Nations seat as one obvious gesture. Taiwan has refused.
Taiwan and China were separated by a civil war in 1949, when the Chinese Nationalist government and army, defeated by the communists, fled into exile on the island.
Both governments say they want Taiwan's reunification with the mainland, but on very different terms. The draft aims to put those differences on the negotiating table.
"The party does not set any conditions," Lin Yu-hsiang, deputy director of the party's policy coordination committee, was quoted by the radio as saying.
"We are only offering a basis for discussion."
Party officials were not available for comment.
Beijing, which sees Taiwan as a renegade province, threatens to recover the island by force if it seeks independence.
